newsitem.title: ARMENIA: Armenian president clamps down on opposition.
newsitem.headline: Armenian president clamps down on opposition.

text.p: Armenian President Levon Ter-Petrosyan brought light tanks and hundreds of armed soldiers into the centre of the capital Yerevan on Thursday in a crackdown on political opponents.

Police raided opposition headquarters and arrested several people after clashes on Wednesday between riot police and protestors who accuse Ter-Petrosyan of rigging last Sunday's presidential election.

Unofficial final results showed Ter-Petrosyan, who has led Armenia since it won independence from the Soviet Union in 1991, with 52.09 percent of votes cast to 41.07 percent for Vazger Manukyan, but opposition supporters say the vote was rigged.
A doctor said one soldier died in hospital after the fighting and dozens of civilians were treated for injuries.

This correspondent saw armoured vehicles and troops with Kalashnikov automatic rifles sealing off the central Republic Square, near Manukyan's headquarters. Other central streets were sealed by hunderds of armed soldiers who stopped every pedestrian.
Manukyan's two-storey building was surrounded by security officers who refused to answer questions. The whereabouts of Manukyan, whose supporters say he won the poll, was not immediately known.
The square was quiet and there was no violence there.
But Reuters Television producer Nino Ivanishvili witnessed a police raid on the headquarters of a small opposition party not far from the square.

"Armed people in camouflage broke into the building. They were dragging people out and punching and kicking them," she said. She saw at least seven severely beaten men being dragged into a police van.

Thursday's clampdown followed an announcement from Ter-Petrosyan that he had banned all rallies and demonstrations would punish all "provocateurs". He blamed them for clashes outside the parliament building on Wednesday night.

"In accordance with the constitution, I announce that all meetings, demonstrations and gatherings are forbidden without our permission," Ter-Petrosyan said on national television in the early hours of Thursday.
"We will take other legal measures if needed. The provocateurs will be punished. We won't allow the very existence of Armenia...to be put into danger."
Police on Wednesday fired over the heads of a crowd which stormed the parliament grounds in Yerevan during protests about Ter-Petrosyan's victory.
The protesters say the vote was rigged to defeat former prime minister Manukyan. They hurled bricks and police waded in with truncheons.
